title: Devissage of a property of coherent sheaves over the integral closed subschemes of a Noetherian scheme
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme], i.e. locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and let $\mathcal P$ be a property of coherent $\mathcal O_X$-modules [pqf-def-coherent]. For a sheaf of ideals $\mathcal J\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ and an $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal G$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] let $\mathcal J\mathcal G\subseteq\mathcal G$ be the image of the multiplication map $\mathcal J\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal G\to\mathcal G$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]; stalks $\mathcal G_x$ are as in [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk], $\mathfrak m_x\subset\mathcal O_{X,x}$ is the maximal ideal of the local ring [def-weil-residue-field], and $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal G)=\{x\in X:\mathcal G_x\neq0\}$ [def-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base](2). Assume: (0) $\mathcal P$ holds for the zero module; (1) for every short exact sequence $0\to\mathcal F_1\to\mathcal F\to\mathcal F_2\to0$ of coherent $\mathcal O_X$-modules, if $\mathcal F_1$ and $\mathcal F_2$ have $\mathcal P$ then so has $\mathcal F$; (2) if $\mathcal F$ is coherent and $\mathcal P$ holds for $\mathcal F^{\oplus r}$ for some $r\ge1$, then $\mathcal P$ holds for $\mathcal F$; (3) for every closed immersion $i:Z\to X$ [def-weil-closed-immersion] with $Z$ an integral scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme] and every point $\xi\in X$ whose closure $\overline{\{\xi\}}$ is $i(Z)$ (the generic point of $Z$), there is a coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal G$ such that (a) $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal G)=i(Z)$, (b) $\mathfrak m_\xi\mathcal G_\xi=0$, and (c) for every quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals $\mathcal J\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ with $\mathcal J_\xi=\mathcal O_{X,\xi}$ there is a coherent sub-$\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal G'\subseteq\mathcal J\mathcal G$ with $\mathcal G'_\xi=\mathcal G_\xi$ (as submodules of $\mathcal G_\xi$) such that $\mathcal P$ holds for $\mathcal G'$. Then $\mathcal P$ holds for every coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module.

proof.text: Prove coherence transport under isomorphisms from [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth], transporting finite local generating families along the isomorphism. A coherent kernel of an identity is zero by [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-kernel-cokernel-locnoeth]. Apply extension closure to 0→0→F→G→0 to obtain P-invariance under isomorphisms. For a finite filtration with coherent terms and P on each cokernel, use the short exact sequence for each mono and its cokernel, induct over Fin(m+1), and transport from the top subobject to F. This includes m=0.

Use sectionwise injectivity and [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-exact] to show support of a subobject is contained in the ambient support; use its surjective cokernel stalk map to show the same for a quotient. Isomorphisms give equal supports. For a nonzero ideal on an integral closed subscheme, [lem-weil-pbc-integral-scheme-ideal-generic-stalk] makes its generic stalk nonzero and [lem-weil-pbc-closed-pushforward-stalks] does the same for its pushforward. The pushforward support is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-module-support-closed] and contained in the closed image by the off-image stalk formula, so it equals that image.

Induct on every closed subset T using the Mathlib well-founded order on Closeds(X) in [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-scheme-closed-subsets-minimal]. The induction claim is: every ideal pushforward from every integral closed immersion whose image is contained in T has P. For one such i:Z→X, take ξ=i(η), whose closure is i(Z) by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-sober] and the closed embedding. For coherent Q supported in i(Z) and vanishing at ξ, take [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-filtration-integral-subschemes]. Step 2 puts every integral quotient support inside Supp(Q). It is strictly smaller than i(Z), since ξ belongs to i(Z) and does not belong to Supp(Q). Its closed image is strictly smaller than T. The induction hypothesis, isomorphism invariance, and step 1 give P(Q).

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-property-integral-ideals-of-small-support] to the chosen i and ξ, supplying step 3 for its small-support hypothesis and the original integral hypothesis for its distinguished module. This finishes the induction claim for T.

For any coherent F, take [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-filtration-integral-subschemes] once more. Each cokernel is coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-kernel-cokernel-locnoeth], isomorphic to an ideal pushforward. Apply the induction claim at T=X to every quotient, transport P across its isomorphism, and apply step 1 to the finite filtration.

proof_origin.place: 01YM via 01YL and 01YF: Lean proves the filtration assembly, support inclusions and equality, and well-founded closed-support induction; only the generic-point annihilator and ideal-intersection step is isolated as lem-weil-pbc-coherent-property-integral-ideals-of-small-support. Original zero hypothesis and target signatures are retained.
